name: Robert Maxwell
role: British media proprietor (Pergamon Press, Mirror Group) and Labour MP for Buckingham (1964–1970)
summary: Maxwell sat as a Labour backbencher from 1964 to 1970, where his recorded positions were pro-technology and planning-minded on economics, strongly in favour of Britain joining the European Community, hostile to an independent British nuclear deterrent, and critical of the 1968 Soviet invasion of Czechoslovakia while urging that detente be kept. Little of his stated political thinking from his later career as a publisher and newspaper owner is available in his own words, so most statements have no recorded position.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Contested: backed Britain joining the European Communities (10 May 1967), but also argued that supranationality had ended with Hallstein's resignation; he did not speak to pooling sovereignty itself.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: In the 6 April 1965 Commons debate he called the TSR2 a product of the former government's 'stupid desire' to keep a 'so-called independent nuclear deterrent' and welcomed its cancellation.

party-own-road.rationale: In the 26 August 1968 debate he called the Soviet invasion illegal and treacherous and described the Czech party's pending conference as set to clear out Stalinists and renew itself, which the Russians opposed because they wanted orders taken from the top. He sided with the Czech party deciding its own course, though he did not state the general principle.

defeat-communism.rationale: In the 26 August 1968 Commons debate on the invasion of Czechoslovakia he condemned the Soviet invasion but warned against using it to revive the cold war, said it would be wrong to abandon detente, and opposed turning the Czech cause into a weapon for stiffening NATO against the Warsaw Pact. This points to coexistence and detente, not defeating communism.

notes: Searches of his Hansard contributions (1964–1970) found speeches mainly on technology, aviation, air pollution, parliamentary catering and the economy, with few statements that match the test's statements. His later statements as a newspaper owner were not found in primary form, and positions attributed to him in secondary accounts (for example on the miners' strike or on Israel) were not used.
